tasks.name: A Special Morning
tasks.text: It is Saturday, the seventh of October. Today is Ollie's birthday! He wakes up early and runs to the kitchen. On the table there is a big box. Inside Ollie finds a new football — a gift from Mum and Dad. Sophie gives him a colourful album for drawings. Jack gives him a small robot. Ollie is very happy: Thank you! Buddy runs into the room with a paper bow on his collar, and Bella sits on Ollie's chair and purrs. It is a wonderful morning!

tasks.name: Invitations
tasks.text: After breakfast Ollie writes invitations for his friends. He draws small cards with a ball and writes: You are invited to my birthday party! Come on Sunday at three o'clock. Sophie draws colourful balloons on every card. Ollie makes four invitations: for George and Emily from upstairs, for Sam and for his cousin Harry. Buddy wants to take one card to the neighbours himself — he puts it in his teeth and runs to the door. Everyone laughs: Buddy is the best postman!

tasks.name: The Guests
tasks.text: On Sunday the guests come at three o'clock. George and Emily bring a big box with a game. Sam gives Ollie a toy aeroplane that he made himself. And cousin Harry arrives with a basketball: We will play in the summer! The children play, draw posters and run in the courtyard with Buddy. Mrs. Carter and Mum make tea. Mrs. Green brings her famous biscuits. At four o'clock everyone sits at the table.

tasks.name: The Cake
tasks.text: At four o'clock Mum brings the birthday cake. There are ten candles on it. The lights go off, and everyone sings: Happy birthday to you! Ollie closes his eyes, makes a wish and blows out the candles — one, two, three... ten! Hurray! Ollie cuts the cake: the first piece goes to Mum, the second to Dad, and then to all the guests. Emily says quietly: Your cake is the most delicious in the world. Ollie smiles: That is because Mum baked it with love. This is a real holiday!

tasks.name: Good Night, Birthday!
tasks.text: In the evening the guests go home. Ollie is tired but very happy. He puts the presents on the shelf: the football, the game, the aeroplane and the basketball. Then he writes thank-you cards for his friends. Mum says: Ten years old — how big you are! Ollie hugs his parents: Thank you for the best birthday! Buddy sleeps near the bed, and today he dreams not about football, but about cake. It was a wonderful day. Good night!

tasks.name: Let's Decorate!
tasks.text: December comes, and the first snow falls. In the evening the Carters come down, and everyone decorates the flat together. Mr. Carter brings a box of garlands and lights. The children hang paper snowflakes on the windows. Sophie cuts a big star, and Emily paints it gold. Mum makes hot tea with honey, and Bella watches us from the sofa. When everything is ready, Dad turns off the light. The room shines and looks like a fairy tale!

tasks.name: A Letter to Santa
tasks.text: On Saturday the children write letters to Santa Claus. Ollie writes: Dear Santa, I want a big puzzle and new boots for football. Please bring something for Buddy and Bella too. Emily draws a picture for Santa: her letter is one beautiful snowflake. George asks for a book about dinosaurs. Then they put the letters in a big envelope and hang it on the door. Jack laughs: The postman will be surprised! Mrs. Carter smiles: Every year we write letters too. It is a warm family tradition.

tasks.name: Shopping for Presents
tasks.text: On Sunday the family goes shopping. The streets are full of lights and music. In the shop there are so many toys! Dad asks: What do you want to buy for Grandma? Sophie chooses a warm scarf, and Jack chooses a book about old cars for Grandpa. Ollie looks at a big teddy bear for Emily. Mum buys food for the festive table: fruit, sweets and a big box of biscuits. Then the family drinks hot chocolate in a small café. It is cold outside, but everyone is warm and happy.

tasks.name: The Christmas Tree
tasks.text: On the twentieth of December Dad brings a real Christmas tree. It smells of the forest. Jack carries the tree, and Ollie holds the door. Then the whole family decorates it: red balls, golden stars and small toys from Grandma. Sophie puts her old paper angel on the top of the tree. Emily brings a snowman toy. Mr. Carter says: In Australia, Christmas is in summer — we swim and eat ice cream! Everyone smiles. Mrs. Green brings candy canes. Now the tree is ready — and the holiday is almost here!

tasks.name: The Festive Menu
tasks.text: In the kitchen Mum and Grandma are writing the menu for the New Year. Grandma says: We need a big pie with apples. Mum adds: And salad, and fish from the market. The children ask for pizza, but the parents laugh. In the end the menu has many dishes: salad, soup, pie, fruit and sweets. Ollie draws the menu on a big paper and decorates it with a snowflake. Now the fridge is full, and everyone is waiting for the holiday. What is your favourite dish?

tasks.name: The Festive Table
tasks.text: On the thirty-first of December the family cooks all day. Dad and Jack make a big salad, and Mum bakes a pie. Sophie sets the table: white plates, tall glasses and forks. Ollie puts tangerines in a big bowl — there are always tangerines for New Year! Grandma and Grandpa arrive in the evening and bring their apple pie. The Carters come too, with biscuits. At eight o'clock everything is ready: the table, the tree and a lot of presents under it. Now the holiday can begin!

tasks.name: Twelve O'clock
tasks.text: Five minutes before midnight everyone stands around the tree. The clock on the wall goes tick-tock. Dad turns on the TV, and the President speaks. The children hold their glasses of juice. Then the clock strikes twelve! Hurray! Happy New Year! Everyone says: Happiness, health and good luck! Mum and Dad hug, and Grandma has happy tears in her eyes. Outside fireworks light up the sky. Ollie runs to the window: Look, look! And Buddy barks at the fireworks. The new year has come!

tasks.name: Presents
tasks.text: After midnight comes Ollie's favourite part — presents! Everyone gives and gets gifts under the tree. Grandpa gives Ollie a wooden boat that he made himself. Grandma gives the children warm socks and sweets. The Carters give the family a big box of English tea and a book about London. Sophie gives her parents a picture, and Jack gives everyone his own computer game about the family. Everyone says: It is the best game in the world! Then it is time to try all the new things and play together.

tasks.name: Winter Games
tasks.text: On the second of January the city is white. The snow is deep. The children go to the park with Buddy, George and Emily. They build a big snowman: Jack makes the body, the children make the head, and Ollie gives the snowman his old scarf. Mr. Carter and Dad bring sledges, and everyone rides down the hill. Emily falls into a snowdrift and laughs: I am a snowflake! Buddy runs and jumps through the snow like a puppy. Sophie draws the winter park. In the evening the snowman stands in the park with his scarf and smiles.

tasks.name: Holidays End
tasks.text: On the eighth of January the holidays are almost over. The tree is still shining, but school starts tomorrow. Ollie puts his new football boots next to the door. Jack checks his bag, and Sophie chooses new pencils for art school. In the evening the Carters come down. Emily says: I do not want the holidays to end. Mum smiles: But after every holiday, a new happy day comes. Ollie smiles: Tomorrow I will see George at school! Then everyone looks at the photos and remembers the warm celebrations.

tasks.name: Christmas Morning
tasks.text: On the twenty-fifth of December the Carters invite the family to celebrate Christmas. In the morning Ollie runs upstairs with a small present for Emily. The Carters' flat smells of cinnamon and oranges. Near the window there is a big tree with stockings — long socks with small presents inside. Emily shows Ollie her stocking: chocolate, a little doll and an orange. Mrs. Carter brings Christmas pudding. Everything is new and interesting for Ollie. It is like a fairy tale!

tasks.name: Christmas Dinner
tasks.text: At two o'clock everyone sits at the table. On the table there is a big turkey with vegetables and potatoes. Mrs. Carter says: In Australia we had Christmas in summer — with a barbecue and cold lemonade. But now I like the winter Christmas more! Mr. Carter tells about Christmas in London: the streets are bright, and people sing songs in the squares. Grandma says: Every country has its own traditions, and that is wonderful. After dinner everyone plays board games. Mr. Carter wins for the first time!

tasks.name: A Walk in the Snow
tasks.text: After dinner the two families go for a walk. The park is white and quiet. The snow creaks under the boots. George and Ollie make snowballs and throw them at Dad — he laughs and runs away. Emily and Sophie build a small snow cat, and Jack takes a photo. Mr. Carter sees a bird on a branch: In winter, birds need our help. The children give the bird some bread. Then everyone goes home and drinks hot tea with biscuits. It is a real Christmas!

tasks.name: Gifts and Wishes
tasks.text: In the evening the Carters give the family Christmas presents. Mum gets a warm English scarf, and Dad gets a book about London. The children get English sweets and a game about travels. Ollie gives Mr. Carter a drawing: a snowman with a top hat. Sophie gives Mrs. Carter her picture of the winter park. Emily gives the family a card with the words: Thank you for the best year! Everyone is very happy. Presents are not important — attention and friendship are.

tasks.name: The Best Holiday
tasks.text: At home Ollie cannot fall asleep. The whole day was like one big present. He thinks about the stockings, the pudding and the snowman. Mum comes into his room: Did you like the English Christmas? Yes! But our New Year is warmer. Mum laughs: One day you will visit London and see everything yourself. Ollie dreams: Maybe George and I will celebrate Christmas there together. Sleep well, my dear. Sweet dreams! It was the best holiday in his life — because he celebrated it with his family and his friends.
